chapter: Charlie Johnson, Willie Gant and the late 1920s
title: Pipe and straight soprano saxophones; Hodges and Bechet
summary: There are two kinds of soprano sax; Hodges played it like Bechet and shared Caldwell's birthday.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone

blocks.x: Well, you know, the soprano is a peculiar instrument. A lot of people don't know it, but there are two different sopranos. The pipe model and the straight model --
But the pipe model had the most muted more sweeter tone than the straight model.
But then Johnny Hodges told me that chest Curved you could shoot more on the closed one.
You could. Johnny played a lot. If he'd have stayed on it, Johnny (unintelligible) played the horn like --
-- Bechet, because Bechet brought him here from Boston, you know. And he was -- we used to kid Johnny about it, (unintelligible) going to happen when I want dont to
play it because him and I were born on the same birthday, same day.
